Adding a security checklist to the thread — high-level items we'll evaluate for any private observability intake: 

- Authentication: prefer mTLS client certs for collector-to-redwood ingestion endpoints where possible. If not, short-lived bearer tokens provisioned via your identity vendor (OIDC) are acceptable.
- Authorization: collectors should be scoped to per-cluster credentials; avoid cluster-wide tokens that cover multiple customers/tenants.
- Egress: list of Redwood egress IPs + FQDNs (we'll provide a CIDR block); consider an outbound proxy or NAT gateway pattern.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ with server cert pinning; we support custom trust stores in private deployments.
- Proof/evidence: retention of delivery logs for 90 days for SOC audits; recommend enabling delivery acknowledgements and storing to your SIEM.
- SIEM integration: if you want to forward to Splunk, we can accept HEC endpoints or provide a forwarder inside VPC that pushes to your SIEM via a peered route.

I'll attach our standard security questionnaire — answer the telemetry/ingest sections and I can mark any hard blockers.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Platform Security

Thanks for the fast follow and the answers — this is exactly what we needed. Summary of findings, decisions, and next steps: 

Summary (short)
- Collector choices: Vector for logs, OTel for traces — both are compatible. We'll validate a Vector sink + OTel exporter in the PoC.
- Egress/proxy: ACME must use their corporate HTTP proxy; Redwood will support ingestion behind a proxy. We need the proxy TLS interception behavior documented to validate cert chains.
- Auth: primary plan = mTLS where possible; fallback = short-lived bearer tokens via OIDC.
- SIEM: two options: Redwood provides an internal forwarder inside the customer's VPC (preferred for strict networks) OR Redwood accepts HEC pushes if ACME can open egress from a secure forwarder.
- Retention/audit: Redwood will keep delivery/audit logs for 90 days by default; for the 365-day legal requirement, ACME will mirror archives to Splunk. We'll produce a mirror runbook.

Action items (owners / ETA)
- Redwood (Monica): produce connector compatibility matrix and a minimal PoC checklist for Vector + OTel — ETA 2027-05-18.
- Redwood (Vivek): provide CIDR/FQDN allowlist and spec for mTLS provisioning + security questionnaire review — ETA 2027-05-17.
- ACME (ops): provide a short sample of proxy TLS behavior (does it MITM / re-sign certs) and confirm ability to run an internal forwarder — ETA 2027-05-18.
- Joint: schedule a 60‑minute PoC kickoff (we propose 2027-05-20) to run a sample trace and log through the chosen path.

Next steps / links
- I've created a shared folder for artifacts and a Jira ticket to track the PoC: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_shared_ObsvPlan
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INFRA-2147
